answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before transacting, and weigh influence by bonded stake rather than account count. A vertex in the trust graph gains reach through repeated, independently verified exchanges; a ledge of accounts cannot boost itself with circular endorsements, since those add no weight. Audits at dawn can expose fraud and burn bonds. To mount a sybil attack, an adversary must lock real capital for every identity and risk losing it, making mass accounts costly instead of free.
